$comment: Reviewable input for scripts/voices/generate.mjs. Every `text` is the exact on-screen caption. Neural engine only (phonation/whispered effects are rejected by Polly neural, so a whisper is soft volume + slow rate). `rate` and `pauseMs` shape the 1930s telephone cadence.

lines.speaker: caller-ruth
lines.text: Operator. Put me where the clock rang after midnight.

lines.speaker: caller-ruth
lines.text: Put me where the clock rang after midnight.

lines.speaker: caller-ruth
lines.text: Do not place me beside the orchard. Something there has learned my voice.

lines.speaker: caller-ruth
lines.text: I did not die indoors, operator. Do not file me with the cold ones.

lines.speaker: caller-amos
lines.text: Operator. Forty winters I dug that hill. Find me a place where the ground is mine.

lines.speaker: caller-amos
lines.text: Forty winters on that hill, operator. I want the ground, not a roof over me.

lines.speaker: caller-amos
lines.text: No cold drawers, no standing water, and the chapel door was always shut to me.

lines.speaker: caller-amos
lines.text: The bell tower belongs to Ruth Bell. Leave me the apple trees.

lines.speaker: caller-tobias
lines.text: Operator. The river kept the ferry and let go of the bell. Ring me through.

lines.speaker: caller-tobias
lines.text: I went under at the mill race. Put me where the water still stands.

lines.speaker: caller-tobias
lines.text: Not the orchard, not the drawers, not the chapel. None of them are wet.

lines.speaker: caller-tobias
lines.text: The tower already has its operator. Do not ring me there.

lines.speaker: caller-ines
lines.text: Operator. Nine beds on my ward and I counted every one. Count me last.

lines.speaker: caller-ines
lines.text: Nine beds on my ward, and I counted them all. Count me last.

lines.speaker: caller-ines
lines.text: No bells, no weather, no psalms. I want it quiet.

lines.speaker: caller-ines
lines.text: Amos Kettle goes in before me. He always did the heavy lifting.

lines.speaker: caller-ines
lines.text: And keep me out of the water. I have seen what it does.

lines.speaker: line-13
lines.text: Operator. You never wrote down who placed the first call.

lines.speaker: line-13
lines.text: I can hear every cord you pull, operator.

lines.speaker: line-13
lines.text: Each wrong jack is a letter in my name.

lines.speaker: line-13
lines.text: Stop listening to them. Listen to me.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: In the nineteen-thirties, every call went through a person. LINE 13 brings that switchboard back, and the dead are calling.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: You listen. You read the clue. You plug the cord. Each caller has exactly one place they belong, and the clues are enough to find it.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: A wrong route is not a game over. It crosses a line. Another voice cuts in. Something else starts to listen.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Every mistake costs you the room. But the last clue each caller gives is a whisper that only comes after a crossed line, so a mistake never leaves you stuck.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: When the last line closes, your routes draw a ritual. Your ending depends on how many lines you crossed. There are three.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: It plays with the keyboard alone, with the sound off, with motion reduced, and on a phone.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Behind every connection is a graph. Before an episode ships, a solver proves it has exactly one answer, and that no move can trap you. This one: one solution, three thousand five hundred states checked, zero dead ends.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: I built it with Kiro. A spec said no move may trap the player. Steering rules became checks that fail on save. And a property test found a bug in my own solver that every hand-written test had missed.

narration.speaker: narrator
narration.text: Night Operator is a Kiro Crew app. Six agents write an episode. The game's own solver rejects the first draft, sends it back, and only the fixed one ships.
